Independent civic data project

Where revenue comes from

Every revenue stream in the Town's Budget Supplements, 2018 through 2027: what each source was estimated to bring in, what it did, what has come in so far this year, and what the 2027 Tentative expects.

Independent project·Updated September 26, 2026·● Current·Check data freshness →
💡In plain English
The General Fund estimated its outside revenue below what came in for 5 years running, 2021–2025, by $22,713,810 in all. The 2027 Tentative expects $13,343,312 from those sources, against $16,382,426 collected in 2025.
  • ›Why it matters: every dollar of revenue the budget does not count has to be raised by the tax levy instead. When estimates run low year after year, the difference lands in fund balance.
  • ›Estimated, not set: the levy and planned use of fund balance are decisions, not forecasts, and money moved between the Town’s own funds is bookkeeping. They are kept apart from “outside revenue” throughout.
  • ›Before the audit: collections are the Town’s books as the Supplements print them, before each year’s audit.
Property tax levy
$54.34M
75% of the 2027 General Fund · Set by the Board, within the tax cap
Outside revenue
$13.34M
19% of the 2027 General Fund · Fees, interest, state aid, sales and cannabis taxes, PILOTs and more
From other Town funds
$3.38M
5% of the 2027 General Fund · Charges and transfers from the Town’s own districts
Fund balance used
$0.95M
1% of the 2027 General Fund · Savings from earlier years

General Fund: estimate against result

Outside revenue only: everything but the tax levy, fund balance, and money from the Town's own funds. In 5 of the 7 years on file, more came in than the budget counted on.

The Community Preservation Fund's “Other Non Property Taxes” is the 2% Peconic Bay land-transfer tax. State law limits it to community preservation — open space, farmland, historic places and, in part, water quality — so money it collects above its estimate cannot lower the tax levy.

Every revenue account in the Town's Budget Supplements, 2020 through 2027. Each Supplement prints what was collected two years earlier, the prior year's estimate and its collections through June 30, and the new request and Tentative, so together they give collections for 2018-2025 beside the estimate for each year. Collections are the Town's books before the audit. Built from the 8 Supplements, 2020–2027; the newest is the 2027 Budget Supplement (PDF). Categories follow New York's uniform revenue codes. The 2021 and 2022 Supplements print no department request for revenue.

Independent. Source-first. Built for residents.

Riverhead Budget Live is not affiliated with the Town of Riverhead. Important figures should be checked against the linked official record. Google Analytics is used to understand aggregate site usage; no account is required to use the site.
